nodes.label: Submit Your Show Feature
nodes.rationale: Replaces the disconnected Google Form so band pitches live in-app instead of a separate spreadsheet workflow.

nodes.label: No-Online-Payment v1 Model
nodes.rationale: Confirmed: no online payment processing in v1 — a reservation only holds a spot, the guest pays cash or InstaPay at the cafe on the day.

nodes.label: Server-Enforced Authorization
nodes.rationale: Authorization is enforced on the server in app/staff/layout.tsx, app/admin/layout.tsx, and every API route via lib/rbac.ts — there is no middleware gate to bypass.

nodes.label: Continue as Guest State
nodes.rationale: Neither reference mockup showed a guest option, but idea.md requires Login/Sign Up/Continue as Guest, so a lower-emphasis text link was added beneath the social buttons to reconcile the two.

nodes.label: Brand-Derived Photography Fallback
nodes.rationale: No real Dekka interior/event photography exists yet, so photo slots fall back to a brand-derived treatment (warm pendant-light gradients + tatreez texture) rather than shipping stock photography that isn't actually Dekka.

nodes.label: Border Radius Scale (12-14px app vs 4px --radius-brand workspace)
nodes.norm_label: border radius scale (12-14px app vs 4px --radius-brand workspace)

nodes.label: Theme Flip via .dk-workspace
nodes.rationale: Each shared UI primitive has one class whose colors change automatically inside a .dk-workspace ancestor, so the same Card component renders dark on the public site and cream in the admin dashboard without building it twice.

nodes.label: Sharp Workspace vs Soft App Rationale
nodes.norm_label: sharp workspace vs soft app rationale
nodes.rationale: The brand's 'sharp cream workspace vs. soft dark app' contrast is a deliberate design decision that gets diluted if the two start borrowing each other's radius values, so --radius-brand is kept as its own named token instead of reusing Tailwind defaults.

nodes.label: Staff/Admin Light Workspace Exception
nodes.rationale: Door check-in and admin dashboard are back-office, data-entry-heavy tools used at a counter; a lighter, higher-contrast cream/white theme is easier to read and enter data into quickly than the dark theme.

nodes.label: Two Surfaces, One Palette
nodes.rationale: Rather than threading a tone prop through every shared component, primitives flip color automatically inside a .dk-workspace ancestor so one Card renders dark on the public app and cream in the back-office.

nodes.label: Cairo / Plus Jakarta Sans Font Families
nodes.norm_label: cairo / plus jakarta sans font families

nodes.label: 'Dekka' = Bench Meaning
nodes.rationale: Dekka (دكة) means bench/seating platform, baked directly into copy like the sign-up hero line 'Take your place on the bench' so the brand name becomes an invitation rather than just a logo.

nodes.label: Arabic-First Copywriting Principle
nodes.rationale: Arabic is drafted first as the primary voice, then an English line is written to carry the same warmth rather than a literal translation, since a flat literal translation of a warm Arabic line usually reads stiff in English.

nodes.label: Dekka Coffee Shop Banner (public brand asset)
nodes.norm_label: dekka coffee shop banner (public brand asset)

nodes.label: Site-Wide Dark 'Coffeehouse at Night' Theme
nodes.rationale: Recommended across the whole public app because it matches the live-music-venue side of Dekka's identity better than a bright daytime cafe look, and it's what's already fully designed in the auth mockups.

nodes.label: Dekka Data Model (User, Event, Reservation, CheckIn, BandSubmission)
nodes.norm_label: dekka data model (user, event, reservation, checkin, bandsubmission)

nodes.label: Deliberately Out of Scope for v1
nodes.norm_label: deliberately out of scope for v1
nodes.rationale: Online payments, loyalty points, non-event table reservations, push notifications, waitlists, and QR check-in are excluded to keep v1 shippable.

nodes.label: Known Gaps
nodes.rationale: Capacity is checked read-then-write rather than atomically enforced (unlikely double-booking accepted at cafe scale); next.config.ts allows images from any HTTPS host pending a settled image host.

nodes.label: Warm vs. Plain Copy Rule
nodes.rationale: Hero headlines, empty states, confirmations, and the About page stay warm/invitational; transactional copy (form labels, errors, admin/staff tool copy) stays plain and clear.

nodes.label: Bilingual Label Pattern (English / العربية)
nodes.rationale: English first, forward slash, Arabic second, always on one line, wrapped in dir="ltr" with each half tagged lang — this is the visual identity of the whole app, echoing the دكة / Dekka lockup in the logo.

nodes.label: 'COFFEE SHOP' Tagline
nodes.rationale: The real tagline pulled from the banner; an earlier placeholder mockup's fabricated 'COFFEE & COMMUNITY' circle badge does not exist in the real brand and should never be reintroduced.

nodes.label: brand:assets Generation Pipeline
nodes.rationale: npm run brand:assets turns IMGS/ originals into public/brand/* so the transparent-PNG requirement from authorization-UI.md §1 is reproducible via script rather than a manual export.

nodes.label: Component Reuse Checklist
nodes.rationale: Before styling a new screen from scratch, check whether it's really just PageHeader + Card + TextField/Field + Button + Badge — almost every screen in Dekka is built from that same handful of pieces.

nodes.label: Dark-Ink-On-Dark-Background Rule
nodes.rationale: The logo is dark brown ink and nearly disappears on ink-black, so every appearance on a dark surface sits inside a cream rounded-plate badge; the raw logo file should never be placed directly on a dark background without it.

nodes.label: Hand-Rolled UI Primitives
nodes.rationale: UI primitives are hand-rolled in components/ui/ rather than generated by the shadcn CLI because the brand (cream paper, coffee ink, 4px corners, no shadows, RTL) is specific enough that generated neutral components would have been overridden anyway.

nodes.label: lib/constants.ts Shared Enums
nodes.rationale: Client components import enums from lib/constants.ts (no runtime deps) rather than from @/models/*, so the MongoDB driver never gets pulled into the browser bundle.

nodes.label: @layer components Gotcha
nodes.rationale: The .dk-* primitive classes must live inside @layer components — otherwise the padding shorthand in .dk-field outranks Tailwind's ps-11 utility and leading icons overlap input text.
